starting-off-talking-to-timfraku.speaker: Timfraku
starting-off-talking-to-timfraku.text: I am the Chief of Tai Bwo Wannai Village! Who dares set foot in my hut?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Well then adventurer, you would do better to rove elsewhere.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Well then explorer, you would do better to travel elsewhere.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Well then wayfarer, you would do better to wander elsewhere.

options.text: Who me? Oh I'm just a nobody.

steps.player: Who me? Oh I'm just a nobody.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Well then NoBody, you would do better to go elsewhere.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: This place has been cursed. Our people have angered the gods and have fled the village.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: You ask too many questions. Now begone!

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: You ask too many questions. Now begone!

options.text: Where have your people fled to?

steps.player: Where have your people fled to?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: You ask too many questions. Now begone!

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Trufitus Shakaya? What news does he send?

steps.player: Trufitus has communed with the gods. Your village was never cursed and your people are free to return.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Bwana, do you speak the truth?

steps.player: Yes, I helped Trufitus gather ingredients for a commune potion.

steps.text: Timfraku appears to concentrate very deeply.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Then it must be true.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: I cannot thank you enough for what you have done so far.

options.text: Your gratitude is all I deserve.

steps.player: Your gratitude is all I deserve.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: No, Bwana, you deserve much more.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: I now ask you to do one last thing for our village.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: I ask you to deliver the good news to my three sons Tamayu, Tinsay & Tiadeche, and then return them to the village.

steps.prompt: Start the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Thank you very much. I shall reward you greatly if you succeed.

steps.player: If I succeed? How hard can it be?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: We shall see, Bwana.

steps.player: No, I've had quite enough of the jungle already.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Very well. Return when you are ready.

options.text: Well, some gold would be nice.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: I now ask you to do one last thing for our village.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: It should be clear to anyone that I am the chief of Tai Bwo Wannai. I ensure that things run smoothly in this village.

options.text: Is there anything interesting to do here?

steps.player: Is there anything interesting to do here?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Yes Bwana, plenty of interesting things to do. Firstly you could make an effort to tidy the place up a little. Equip yourself with a machete and start cutting down the jungle that seems to be growing all around here.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Go and have a chat with Murcaily for information, he's tending the hardwood grove to the east of here.

options.text: I've been doing some work around the village.

steps.player: I've been doing some work around the village.

steps.text: If the player has not been doing the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup tasks:

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: That's good Bwana, I would hate to think that you were just being lazy while you're in my kingdom!
If the player has completed at least one task from the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup task list:

starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.speaker: Timfraku
starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.text: Are you ready to help me?

starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.player: What do I have to do?

starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.speaker: Timfraku
starting-off-if-the-player-refused-to-st.text: I ask you to deliver the good news to my three sons Tamayu, Tinsay & Tiadeche, and then return them to the village.

starting-off-talking-to-timfraku-after-s.text: If the player says they are a roving adventurer:

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Welcome back, roving adventurer.

starting-off-talking-to-timfraku-after-s.text: If the player says they are a travelling explorer:

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Welcome back, travelling explorer.

starting-off-talking-to-timfraku-after-s.text: If the player says they are a wandering wayfarer:

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Welcome back, wandering wayfarer.

starting-off-talking-to-timfraku-after-s.text: If the player says they are a "Nobody":

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Welcome back, Nobody.

options.text: Can you tell me more about your sons?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about your sons?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: My first son is Tamayu. After him was born Tinsay. And after him was born Tiadeche.

options.text: Can you tell me more about Tamayu?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Tamayu?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Tamayu was a natural born hunter. He killed his first monkey at the age of three!
Shows initial brother queries

options.text: Can you tell me more about Tinsay?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Tinsay?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Tinsay was brought up to be a priest. Be careful with him - he has acted strange since the accident.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: It involved Jogres. We don't talk about it.
Shows initial brother queries

options.text: Can you tell me more about Tiadeche?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Tiadeche?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Tiadeche always wanted to hunt fish. However, he has not had much success.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: He needs to improve his technique - but he does not heed my advice.
Shows initial brother queries

options.text: Where can I find your sons?

steps.player: Where can I find your sons?

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: On our island of Karamja. They will not have fled far.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: Patience, Bwana, patience.

steps.speaker: Timfraku
steps.text: And good conversation skills.
Shows previous village questions.

starting-off-attempting-to-enter-any-of-.text: You do not have permission to enter here

talking-to-tiadeche.player: Tiadeche, I bring good news. Trufitus has communed with the gods -  your village is once again safe.
Your father requests that you return to the village.

talking-to-tiadeche.speaker: Tiadeche
talking-to-tiadeche.text: I will return only when I have caught a Karambwan.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: You don't know? The Karambwan is a species of octopus native to these waters.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: They have a monopoly on its sale in the pirate town of Brimhaven.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: At this rate, it could take forever.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Sometimes, oblivion is all I crave...

options.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.player: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I just don't know. You can try.

steps.player: What would you have me do?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Something ... helpful?

options.text: How are you fishing for the Karambwan?

steps.player: How are you fishing for the Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I'm trying to catch them with a net as they swim by.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: They keep fighting loose of the twining.

talking-to-tiadeche-talking-to-tiadeche-.text: If the player uses a raw, cooked, or poisoned Karambwan on Tiadeche:

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I refuse to take your offerings. I must catch this Karambwan myself.

talking-to-tiadeche-talking-to-tiadeche-.text: If the player gives Tiadeche an empty Karambwan vessel:

steps.player: Tiadeche, instead of using your net, try using this vessel.

steps.text: You hand over the Karambwan vessel to Tiadeche.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: What is it?

steps.player: It has been specially constructed to catch Karambwan. Once they enter it, they cannot return..

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: As you say, Bwana.
Tiadeche attempts to use the Karambwan vessel.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: This vessel is useless! The Karambwan are not even interested in entering it!
the Karambwan vessel back

talking-to-tiadeche-talking-to-tiadeche-.text: If the player gives Tiadeche a raw Karambwanji:

steps.player: I've been told that the Karambwan feed only on the Karambwanji. This will make good bait.

steps.text: You hand over a raw Karambwanji to Tiadeche.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: The Holy Friend? Bwana, it is sacrilege to feed these fish to Karambwan!
Tiadeche hesitates, then loads the Karambwanji in his net.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: This attracts many more Karambwan, but they still break free of the net.

talking-to-tiadeche-talking-to-tiadeche-.text: If the player gives Tiadeche a Karambwan vessel with a raw Karambwanji inside:

steps.player: Tiadeche, instead of using your net, try using this vessel.

steps.text: You hand over the Karambwan vessel to Tiadeche.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: What is it?

steps.player: It has been specially constructed to catch Karambwan. Once they enter it, they cannot return..
Also, it has been loaded with Karambwanji. The Karambwan will not be able to resist this bait.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: As you say, Bwana.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Bwana! I cannot believe my eyes!

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I, Tiadeche, who would never amount to anything, have managed to trap a Karambwan!

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Let me offer to you my first catch as a sign of gratitude.
Tiadeche hands you his first catch!
a Raw Karambwan (in the inventory or on the ground if no inventory space)

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Hmph ... my father would not care.

steps.player: Speaking of your father, can we make way to the village? He awaits your return.

steps.text: Continues below

steps.player: I have no need for it, Tiadeche.
We must return to the village now.

steps.text: Continues below

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I cannot return just yet. We witness the change of a turning tide. The secrets of the Karambwan are to be unlocked!

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Before I return, I must ask you to do one thing.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Take a Karambwan vessel to my brother Tinsay. He is the academic amongst us. Tell him I have asked him to study it so that we may craft more of its type.

steps.player: Can I have the vessel back then?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I need this to practice with. Why don't you craft another one?

talking-to-tiadeche-subsequent-dialogue-.text: If the player has not received (another?) Karambwan

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I have caught another Karambwan! I think I ought to give it to you.
a raw Karambwan

talking-to-tiadeche-subsequent-dialogue-.speaker: Tiadeche
talking-to-tiadeche-subsequent-dialogue-.text: Have you taken the Karambwan vessel to Tinsay?
If the player has done so:

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Did you ask for crafting instructions as I said?
If the player does not have the crafting manual:

steps.player: I did, but I think I've lost them...

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Well go back and ask him to make another copy!
If the player has the crafting manual:
You hand over the crafting manual to Tiadeche.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Thank you so much. You cannot understand what all of this means to me and our people.

steps.player: Will you return to the village now?

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Yes. I will do as I promised.

steps.player: I am glad to hear this. Let us go.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Not yet. I will stay here a while to catch more Karambwan.

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: I will meet you in the village once you have helped my brothers and spoken to my father.

talking-to-tiadeche-subsequent-dialogue-.text: If the player has not done so:

steps.speaker: Tiadeche
steps.text: Please hurry! Time is of the essence!

talking-to-tamayu.player: Tamayu, I bring good news. Trufitus has communed with the gods -  your village is once again safe.
Your father requests that you return to the village.

talking-to-tamayu.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu.text: I vow upon the blood of my fallen kin that I shall not set foot in that godforsaken village till I have slain the Shaikahan.

talking-to-tamayu.player: You could slay it after we return to the village.

talking-to-tamayu.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu.text: No! Your pitiful whining tires me. Now let me prepare.

options.text: Tell me more of the Shaikahan.

steps.player: Tell me more of the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: A source of indescribable evil. A beast more foul than your dreams could imagine. It hunts the jungle for anything foolish enough to cross its path.

steps.player: Tell me more of the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: It stands a full man's length in height. Its fore claws are sharp enough to rip through metal. In its eyes glow the embers of death.

options.text: How long have you been hunting the Shaikahan?

steps.player: How long have you been hunting the Shaikahan?

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Since before I was born, stranger. It is my destiny.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: When the gods bless me with success. You may join me on my next hunt, but you may not take part.

steps.prompt: Follow Tamayu on the next hunt?

steps.text: Tamayu attempts to defeat the Shaikahan with his bronze spear...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Shaikhan is at present far too agile for me!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I cannot do enough damage with this spear...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... and  it seems to be healing too quickly!

steps.player: Perhaps later, Tamayu, first son of Timfraku.

options.text: I could slay the Shaikahan for you.

steps.player: I could slay the Shaikahan for you.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: You offer to kill the beast for me? Stop this nonsense, lest I kill you first. It is I who must avenge the death of my kin.

options.text: Tell me more of the Shaikahan.
How long have you been hunting the Shaikahan?
Take me on your next hunt for the Shaikahan.

steps.player: Take me on your next hunt for the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Very well, but you must not interfere.

options.text: I could slay the Shaikahan for you.

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player uses the stuffed monkey or monkey corpse on Tamayu before he kills the Shaikahan:

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I'm not going to skin that! In the jungle, we help only those who help us.

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player hands a partially full agility potion on Tamayu before handing the better spear:

steps.player: I've noticed you commenting on the Shaikahan's agility. Try drinking this potion.

steps.text: If the Agility potion does not have four doses:
If the player asks to take them to his next battle:

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I am beginning to match Shaikahan's agility!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I cannot do enough damage ...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... and  it seems to be healing too quickly!

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player uses an iron or better spear on Tamayu:

steps.text: You hand the spear to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.
If the player asks to take them to their next hunt with the iron spear (or better):
A cutscene appears with Tamayu attacking the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Shaikhan is at present far too agile for me!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I can do enough damage ...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... but  it seems to be healing too quickly!

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player hands a partially full agility potion on Tamayu after handing the better spear:

steps.player: I've noticed you commenting on the Shaikahan's agility. Try drinking this potion.

steps.text: If the Agility potion has one dose:
You hand over the agility potion to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I feel much more agile, but I am not sure whether I can match the Shaikahan...
If the Agility potion has two doses:
You hand over the agility potion to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I feel much more agile, but I am not sure whether I can match the Shaikahan...
If the Agility potion has three doses:
You hand over the agility potion to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I feel much more agile, but I am not sure whether I can match the Shaikahan...
If the Agility potion has four doses:

steps.player: Tamayu, I have brought you more agility potion.

steps.text: You hand over the agility potion to Tamayu.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Thank you Bwana. Now I must prepare for my next hunt.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I feel agile enough to finally match the Shaikahan!

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player has brought a better spear and a four-dose Agility potion and wants to join the hunt again:

steps.text: A cutscene appears with Tamayu attacking the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I have matched the Shaikahan in agility! He can no longer avoid my strikes!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I can do enough damage ...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... but  it seems to be healing too quickly!

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player brings a poisoned spear to Tamayu and joins the hunt:

steps.text: A cutscene appears with Tamayu attacking the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I have matched the Shaikahan in agility! He can no longer avoid my strikes!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: I can do enough damage ...

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: ... and  it does seem quite sick! Perhaps another poison would be more effective?

talking-to-tamayu-using-several-items-on.text: If the player brings a poisoned Karambwan spear to Tamayu and joins the hunt:

steps.text: A cutscene appears with Tamayu attacking the Shaikahan.

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: The end approaches, Shaikahan!

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Gods! Witness this triumph!
The cutscene ends as the Shaikahan is defeated.

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.text: I did it! I, Tamayu, first son of Timfraku, did slay the Shaikahan!

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.text: The deaths of my kin have been avenged. You are my witness.

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.player: Worry not - I am your witness. Shall we return to the village now?

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.text: Yes. Go on ahead without me. I have further matters to attend to here.

talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.speaker: Tamayu
talking-to-tamayu-talking-to-tamayu-afte.text: I will meet you in the village once you have helped my brothers and spoken to my father.
If the player uses the monkey corpse on Tamayu:

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: Let me guess - you want me to skin that monkey. Very well: I shall, since you have assisted me.
You hand over the monkey corpse to Tamayu.
Tamayu hands you some monkey skin and bones.
Monkey skin and monkey bones

talking-to-lubufu.speaker: Lubufu
talking-to-lubufu.text: Watch where you're going, young whippersnapper!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well then go away from here!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: It's a whip. Which snaps. Like me. Now leave!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I am Lubufu - the only fisherman who knows the secret of the Karambwan!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: What a foolish question! Now leave!

talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-agai.speaker: Lubufu
talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-agai.text: You again! I thought I told you to go away!

talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-agai.speaker: Lubufu
talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-agai.text: So I see. What would a fool like you want with me?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I am Lubufu, son of Kedoaba, brother of Kedenda and second cousin twice removed of Ibeli!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Kedoaba is my father, the father of Kedenda and second uncle twice removed of Ibeli!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Kedenda is the son of my father, my brother and second cousin twice removed of Ibeli!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Ibeli is the second nephew twice removed of my father, and the second cousin twice removed of myself and my brother!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Alas, no. Focussed and determined in my trade as I was, I never found a suitable wife.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: It is a great shame that the secret of the Karambwan has to die with me.

steps.player: You could tell me the secret...

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Hah! What a stupid thought! The secret is mine and mine alone!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Our island of Karamja. Long ago, before you were even a thought in the back of a mind, I used to play on these beaches with the pebbles and stones.

steps.player: So you didn't have many friends then?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Silence!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: As I grew older the ways of the world became apparent to me, and my attention turned from the rocks of the land to the fish in the sea.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Despite what you might hear, there are plenty of fish in the sea! Especially when they can only be caught by me!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Nowadays I mostly fish for Karambwan and collect their bait. Collecting the bait has become increasingly tiresome, what with my age and health.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: An order of magnitude older than you! What an impudent question! Collecting bait has become hard enough at this age as it is without having to endure the chiding of you young people!

options.text: Which other young people come by here?

steps.player: Which other young people come by here?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Hmm ... nobody I can recall right now.

options.text: What do you use for bait?

steps.player: What do you use for bait?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: That is part of the secret! Why would I tell you?

options.text: I could help collect the bait.

steps.player: I could help collect the bait.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: And why would you help me?

options.text: You sound like you could do with the help.

steps.player: You sound like you could do with the help.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well perhaps you're right. It's nigh time I could do with some help after all.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I have a fair amount of bait left over since last time I collected some, but I will be needing more shortly.

steps.player: Ok. Where can I find the bait? I don't even know what it is!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Patience. I have kept the nature of the Karambwan a closely guarded secret. There is nobody alive who knows more about them than I do. Furthermore, there is nobody alive who even knows how they feed.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You must therefore understand that what I am about to tell you is given in complete trust, and that you are to tell nobody else.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Very well. The Karambwan are a form of octopus native to our island of Karamja. They feed solely on Karambwanji, a brightly coloured fish which also inhabits the coastal waters surrounding the island.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Karambwanji congregate in coastal shoals near the Holy Lake. You will find it easiest to fish for them there.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Just to the south of Tai Bwo Wannai Village. I'm sure you've met the locals already.

steps.player: And what do I use to fish for the bait?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Any small net will do. Return here as soon as you have caught 20 Karambwanji.

options.text: You sound like you need help.

steps.player: You sound like you need help.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: How dare you say such a thing! Be off with you!

options.text: I enjoy collecting meaningless items for people.

steps.player: I enjoy collecting meaningless items for people.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Meaningless? You know nothing of the Karambwan! Now leave!

options.text: You're right. I don't want to help.

steps.player: You're right. I don't want to help.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I didn't for one moment think you did.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: A species of octopus native to the island which I and I alone know how to catch.

options.text: What do you do with your Karambwan?

steps.player: What do you do with your Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I eat what I need and sell the rest to the Shrimp and Parrot restaurant.

steps.player: Where is the Shrimp and Parrot?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You don't know anything do you? Just north of here, in Brimhaven!

options.text: What do you use for bait?

steps.player: What do you use for bait?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: That is part of the secret! Why would I tell you?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: That depends entirely on how it is cooked...

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Novicely cooked Karambwan is often poisonous to large mammals such as humans. If you buy some and cook it, be careful.

options.text: I have come for your soul.

steps.player: I have come for your soul.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well you've wasted your time. My soul is long gone, along with my compassion.

options.text: I'm with the Fishing Guild Anti-Monopoly Department.

steps.player: I'm from the Fishing Guild Anti-Monopoly Department.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: And I'm from the Island Karamja. What do you want?

steps.player: We demand that you hand over the secret of the Karambwan.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Erm ... no.

steps.player: Oh, ok then. It was worth a try.

options.text: Do you have any spare monkey skin lying around?

steps.player: Do you have any spare monkey skin lying around?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Funny you should say that...

steps.player: Why's that? Do you have any?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well, people have been asking me for monkey skins all day!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: But no, I'm out of monkey skin.

options.text: I've heard something about an accident.

steps.player: I've heard something about an accident.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You will want to ask one of the tribesmen. I don't usually talk about it.

talking-to-lubufu-delivering-raw-karambw.speaker: Lubufu
talking-to-lubufu-delivering-raw-karambw.text: Have you retrieved the Karambwanji yet?

steps.text: If the player has all 20 raw Karambwanji:

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Thank you! This should tide me over for the next month.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Hurry along now. I still need [#] more.

steps.player: No, I'm still fishing for them.

steps.text: Well hurry! My reserves are beginning to run low.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Have you retrieved the Karambwanji yet?

steps.text: I still need [#] more.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Thank you! This should tide me over for the next month.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: A species of octopus native to the island which I and I alone know how to catch.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You should really ought to know that by now.

options.text: What do you do with your Karambwan?
What do you use to catch Karambwan?

steps.player: What do you use to catch Karambwan?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well ... since you ask, a specially constructed octopus pot. But don't tell anybody - that's part of the secret!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: My, you're keen aren't you?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: How would you feel about becoming my apprentice?

steps.player: That's a slight change in attitude...

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: As much as I need to protect the secret, I should not carry it to the grave.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You seem a trustworthy type of person. Do you want to train as my apprentice?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I'm glad to hear it. I'm sure the secrets of the Karambwan will be safe with you.
Lubufu teaches you a new fishing technique.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: In our language, Karambwan literally means 'Friend of Karamja.' As a friend of mine I will now show you how to fish for them.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: There are two aspects to fishing for Karambwan. Firstly, you must have the correct bait. Secondly, you must have the correct equipment.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You already know of the Karambwanji, which shoal in the Holy Lake to the south. As I have explained, the Karambwan feed only on the Karambwanji, which are therefore the perfect bait.

steps.player: But what kind of equipment do you use?

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: It is futile to attempt to catch Karambwan with something as basic as a net. They are too strong and vicious to be caught in such a fashion.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I have spent many years designing a specially shaped vessel, into which Karambwan may pass but from which they may not return.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: If this vessel is loaded with Karambwanji, and then repeatedly lowered into a Karambwan shoal, then you should shortly find a Karambwan octopus trapped inside.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: I will now give you a Karambwan fishing vessel with which you can practise. Make sure you do not lose it. Under no circumstance may you give or show this to anybody. Do you understand?
Lubufu hands you a Karambwan vessel.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Feel free to practise on my fishing spot.
1500 Fishing experience and a Karambwan vessel (either on the ground with no inventory or in their inventory with one space)

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: And I'm glad to hear it!

options.text: I've been catching a whole load of Karambwan!

steps.player: I've been catching a whole load of Karambwan!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Look at you - outgrowing your boots already!

options.text: Actually, I've lost my Karambwan vessel.

steps.player: Actually, I've lost my Karambwan vessel.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: You did what!? I hope nobody else has seen it...

steps.player: Don't worry - nobody will find it...

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well you'd better hope for your sake that this shark is never caught!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well you'd better hope for your sake that this Karambwan is never caught!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Well you'd better hope for your sake that it never floats back!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: In the meantime, you can practise with this.
Lubufu hands you a Karambwan vessel.
a Karambwan vessel either on the ground with no inventory or in their inventory with one space

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Don't mention it. I mean that.

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Why?

steps.player: Everybody keeps asking me to run around and do their errands!

steps.speaker: Lubufu
steps.text: Living the hard life of a fisherman now, eh.

talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-afte.speaker: Lubufu
talking-to-lubufu-talking-to-lubufu-afte.text: Ah ... you again. Have you changed your mind yet? Do you want to train as my apprentice?

reaching-tinsay.text: If the player attempts to climb the rocks from the sides:

steps.text: You can't do that from here.

reaching-tinsay.text: If the player falls on the rocks:

steps.text: You fall and hurt yourself.
The player loses 1-6 hitpoints.

reaching-tinsay.text: If the player keeps their balance on the bridge:

steps.text: You manage to keep your balance on the bridge.
The player gains 10 Agility experience.

reaching-tinsay.text: If the player loses their balance on the bridge:

steps.text: You fall!
You just manage to drag your pitiful frame onto the river bank.
Though you nearly drowned in the river!
The player loses 3-15 hitpoints.

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.player: Tinsay, I bring good news. Trufitus has communed with the gods -  your village is once again safe.
Your father requests that you return to the village.

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.speaker: Tinsay
reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.text: I will return only once I have repaired the tribal statue. Bones!!

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.player: So what are you doing here?

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.speaker: Tinsay
reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.text: I'm ... er ... collecting materials to repair the statue with.

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.player: And I suppose you want me to fetch them for you?
You mean you were just sitting here waiting for people to bring you things you need?
And you don't see anything wrong with that?

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.text: Tinsay pauses and then mutters to himself.

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.speaker: Tinsay
reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.text: Hmm ... I think I need banana in Karamjan rum.

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.player: I see. And you're going to use this to repair the statue?

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay.text: If the player uses a baited Karambwan vessel on Tinsay before helping him:

steps.player: Your brother Tiadeche has sent me. He asks you to study this vessel and produce crafting instructions.

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: You first help me, then I'll help you.

reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay-again.speaker: Tinsay
reaching-tinsay-talking-to-tinsay-again.text: Have you found my banana in Karamjan rum yet?

steps.player: Yes, I have it right here.

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: Well, hand it here then.
If the player only has regular Karamjan rum or no rum:

steps.player: Erm ... I think I lost it in the wash.
Uh ... I think I left it in my other trousers.
Actually, my pet monkey ate it.

steps.text: If the player has the Karamjan rum with a whole banana inside:
You hand Tinsay the banana stuffed into Karamjan rum.

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: I can't use this - there is a banana blocking the bottle!

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: Find some way of actually getting the banana inside the bottle.
Tinsay hands you back the Karamjan rum.
If the player has the Karamjan rum with slices of banana inside it:

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: Yes ... that's it! Hits just the spot!

steps.player: What? I thought you needed that for tribal statue repair!

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: I did!

steps.player: Can we return to the village now?

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: Not yet. I need one more thing...

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: I'm thinking...
Tinsay takes a second to ponder.

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: Seaweed ... Yes - a seaweed sandwich will do the trick.

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: Aha! A seaweed in monkey skin sandwich!

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: Yes. Essential.
If the player doesn't have the rum:

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: It's available in any respectable drinking establishment.

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: They grow everywhere!

options.text: ... convince you to return to the village?

steps.speaker: Tinsay
steps.text: Oblige me by fetching my drink.

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.speaker: Tiadeche
post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.text: Hello, Bwana! We three have finally returned to the village!

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.speaker: Tiadeche
post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.text: I wish to reward you in return for helping me.

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.speaker: Tiadeche
post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.text: I have been attempting to cook the Karambwan. As we all know, they are poisonous if not cooked properly.

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.player: Yes. It's how I, or rather Tamayu, killed the Shaikahan.

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.speaker: Tiadeche

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.player: I no longer feel a stranger here.

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.speaker: Tamayu
post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.text: And neither do we, thanks to you. My father has requested I give you something of value.

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.speaker: Tamayu
post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.text: I have not much of worth to give, apart from my fighting technique.
Tamayu trains you in fighting technique.
2,500 Attack and 2,500 Strength experience
Tamayu hands you some kind of spear.
a Karambwan poisoned rune spear

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.speaker: Tamayu
post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.text: This is the one thing I can give. My family have honoured me with this spear. But the honour is truly yours.

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.speaker: Tamayu
post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-ta.text: Take care, Bwana.

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-su.player: Hello, Tamayu, first son of Timfraku.

post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-su.speaker: Tamayu
post-quest-dialogue-with-the-brothers-su.text: Using your new found poison I have been creating spears. Would you like to buy some?

steps.speaker: Tamayu
steps.text: As you wish, stranger.

lSbvTf.speaker: Lubufu
lSbvTf.text: Well the offer remains open. You're the most trustworthy person I have met in a long time.

lSbvTf.speaker: Lubufu
lSbvTf.text: Let me know if you change your mind.
